'''200''' ('''two hundred''') is the [[natural number]] following [[199 (number)|199]] and preceding [[201 (number)|201]].

==In mathematics==
200 is an [[abundant number]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=A005101 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A005101 |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=oeis.org}}</ref> as 265, the sum of its [[proper divisor]]s, is greater than itself.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Abundant Number |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/AbundantNumber.html |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>

The number appears in the [[Padovan sequence]], preceded by [[86 (number)|86]], [[114 (number)|114]], and [[151 (number)|151]] (it is the sum of the first two of these).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000931|title=Sloane's A000931 : Padovan sequence|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-05-28}}</ref>

The sum of [[Euler's totient function]] φ(''x'') over the first twenty-five integers is 200.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A002088 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A002088 |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>

200 is the smallest base 10 unprimeable number – it cannot be turned into a prime number by changing just one of its digits to any other digit.<ref>{{OEIS|A192545}}</ref> It is also a [[Harshad number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A005349|Niven (or Harshad, or harshad) numbers}}</ref>

200 is an [[Achilles number]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A052486|2=Achilles numbers - powerful but imperfect: if n = Product(p_i^e_i) then all e_i > 1 (i.e., powerful), but the highest common factor of the e_i is 1, i.e., not a perfect power}}</ref>
